comments.body:
The locale pin in 70f0b17 is too wide: it also changes how command text is read, and that breaks managed-process ownership for non-ASCII paths.

The pin applies to every host-kit `ps` read, including the `pid=,command=` batch read and `readProcessField('command='/'state=')` ([host-process.ts:200](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.ts#L200)). Only `lstart` needs it. BSD/macOS `ps` escapes non-ASCII argv bytes under `LC_ALL=C`: a process started with `/Users/mich/é/ü` prints that path by default and `/Users/mich/M-CM-)/M-CM-<` under the pin. `listHostProcesses` stays unpinned, so one scan now compares UTF-8 command text with escaped text. In [agent-browser-process-record.ts:161-162](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/platform-web/src/agent-browser-process-record.ts#L161-L162), `first.command === last.command && command === first.command` compares the pinned read with the unpinned list. A managed Chrome or agent-browser process with a non-ASCII argv path (a non-ASCII home dir or `--user-data-dir`) fails that filter, so it is never recorded or cleaned up. The command matchers in `judgeProcessIdentity` ([host-process.ts:789-796](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.ts#L789-L796)) and the app-log and recording matchers see the escaped text too. They then either refuse to signal or report the process as reassigned. Before this PR both reads used the same locale and agreed. The rule the code must satisfy: no command text read by host-kit changes encoding between callers, and every `ps` read whose output contains `lstart` is pinned. The set of sites is the `lstart`-bearing reads, meaning `HOST_PROCESS_IDENTITY_PS_ARGS` (sync and async) and `readProcessField` when the field is `lstart=`. Please add a regression that asserts the `pid=,command=` call carries no `LC_ALL` pin.

Not blocking, and fine to take or leave: the new test checks the env argument on mocked `runCmd` calls and expects every call to be pinned, which locks in the problem above, and no test drives `judgeProcessIdentity` or `stopDaemonProcess` with a legacy-locale record against a C-locale read (for example `mar. 17 nov. 19:42:27 2026` against `Tue Nov 17 19:42:27 2026`, expecting `unverified`). `simulator-boot.ts` already defines `C_LOCALE_ENV` and a C-form `lstart` regex, so this PR adds a third spelling; exporting one from host-kit and importing it there would fix that. `env: { LC_ALL: 'C' }` replaces the whole environment. PATH and HOME do not matter, because `ps` is resolved by absolute path, but dropping TZ changes how `lstart` renders, and a record written under a custom TZ would still count as differing. `psStartTimesLocaleMismatch` only matches C form against non-C form, so two different localized renderings still compare as differing, and the comment should state that legacy-only scope.

Could the fix be smaller? Pin only the `lstart` reads, keep command and state reads on default options, keep the 'unknown' rule for legacy records, and put the C-form check beside `processStartTimesDiffer` so `simulator-boot.ts` can reuse it. Nothing else needs to change first. As an optional follow-up, `isAgentDeviceDaemonProcess` in `daemon-process.ts` could use the same comparison, so a legacy-locale daemon can still be stopped after the upgrade.

The Coverage check is failing, but its log ends mid-run in the react-native companion worker tests with no assertion or error line, so it does not point at this PR. Please re-run it. No conflicts. Before merge, narrow the pin to the `lstart` reads and add the unpinned-command regression. The issue's own reproduction (a French-locale daemon with `LC_TIME=C daemon stop`) has not been run on macOS yet, so a live run of that route showing `daemon stop` finding the daemon would close it.

A separate security cross-check of this head, run because process identity decides which process gets signalled, adds two more items before merge:
- **The pin drops the child environment and changes the identity clock** ([ps-start-time.ts:11](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/host-kit/src/internal/ps-start-time.ts#L11)). An explicit exec env replaces the inherited one, so `ps` loses TZ (and LANG) and renders `lstart` in the host zone. With the same explicit TZ on both sides of an upgrade, the new CLI reads a different start time for the same live PID, and `stopDaemonProcess` returns already-exited, which retires a live daemon's registration. Apply `LC_ALL=C` as a final override on top of the effective child environment instead of replacing it.
- **The legacy-locale guard misses real macOS formats** ([ps-start-time.ts:25](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/host-kit/src/internal/ps-start-time.ts#L25)). Under `nb_NO.UTF-8`, macOS `ps` prints the clock with dots, and other locales omit HH:mm:ss entirely. A record written that way does not match the C-form check, so the two renderings count as different lifetimes and a live daemon is again treated as exited. A mismatch should prove exit only when both values are in the same verified format. Otherwise treat the legacy record as unverified, never as gone. Please add a test with a real localized format that has no colon-separated clock, exercised at the `daemon stop` boundary.

Signal authorization still requires an exact identity match, so neither item lets the CLI signal the wrong process. Both make it give up on a live daemon, which is the orphaning bug #4656 reports, now coming from another direction.

Progress at `7ef7ebb`. The locale override is now limited to start-time reads, keeps the effective child environment, and leaves Unicode command reads unpinned. On macOS, a real daemon started under French `LC_TIME` stopped gracefully from a C-locale client. The worker also verified graceful shutdown at a matching explicit `TZ`, and verified that legacy localized records return `identity-unverified` with the process and registration retained.

The cross-time-zone case remains open. The current C-form timestamp has no time-zone provenance. Coverage on this exact head also reports eager-closure growth from `ps-start-time.ts`; this needs a source fix before merge. The cross-zone run and exact-head checks are still pending.

This review covers f88ff09. The newer head 7ef7ebb changes how the locale pin reaches the spawn environment and will get its own delta review; the time-zone and evidence items below do not depend on it. At f88ff09, the earlier command pin and environment replacement findings are fixed, but birth identity and live validation still need work. The real dotted-clock fixture and full macOS run remain outstanding.

Could the process owner give birth tokens locale- and time-zone-independent, identifiable provenance? Starting a daemon in Pacific/Kiritimati and stopping it with TZ=UTC produces different C-shaped strings for the same PID, so [the comparison](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f88ff09/packages/host-kit/src/internal/ps-start-time.ts#L26) can report a live daemon as exited. Conversely, a recycled PID held by a matching daemon can have the same local clock value and pass [signal authorization](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f88ff09/packages/daemon-contracts/src/daemon-process.ts#L38). Both comparisons must treat old unqualified renderings as unknown unless the original lifetime is independently established; keep argv probes separate.

Please remove the redundant [non-ASCII assertion](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f88ff09/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.test.ts#L226) and cover this through the environment-sensitive process reader and real-child stop test. It compares the same constructed string on both sides and passes even when the command read still has the reported regression.

The [takeover test](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f88ff09/packages/daemon-contracts/src/daemon-process-takeover.test.ts#L182) uses a stub executable and synthetic timestamps, so it does not establish graceful stop or live resource ownership. At the fixed head on macOS, start a real detached daemon under fr_FR.UTF-8 in a fresh state directory, capture its PID and token, and run daemon stop --state-dir <dir> --json under LC_TIME=C; show stopped:true, mode:graceful, and PID exit. Repeat across different TZ values. With a separate pre-fix registration from an actual non-C locale, show typed identity-unverified refusal, a live PID, and retained metadata and lock. Run Apple simulator record start and stop through the daemon and show the recorder stops and releases its resource. If the snapshot change remains, show successive requests across provider locales retain the same live snapshot generation.

Not blocking: these can be taken or left: use a valid 21-digit CIM sample for stale Windows fixtures and remove unreachable platform branches; resolve scoped environment overrides once at spawn; bind an installed UTF-8 locale for the real-child Unicode test; use a recorded nb_NO.UTF-8 dotted-clock value; and keep the existing table case instead of the duplicate one-second reuse assertion.

Could the already loaded process capability own POSIX birth-token construction and its sync and async probe policy, with exec resolving scoped overrides once at spawn and the cancellable snapshot provider reusing that policy? A versioned token could identify comparable clocks while historical raw values remain unknown, preserving Linux /proc and Windows CIM tokens; choosing provenance and the legacy refusal rule at the process boundary comes first, while preserving Apple provider cancellation and routing, removing the extra eager import, and consolidating fixtures. No ADR amendment is needed for that ownership.

[Android Smoke Tests](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/actions/runs/44383605765/job/135082109348) passed, but Linux normally uses /proc and does not exercise macOS lstart. [Repo Guards](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/actions/runs/44383605968/job/135082110025) reports R86 on the added process.env capture, and [Coverage](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/actions/runs/44383605968/job/135082109977?pr=4682) reports ten eager-closure assertions with one extra module each. There are no known conflicts. Before merge, fix birth-token ownership and scope, clear R86 and the eager-closure checks at their source, and provide the exact-head macOS receipts.

At 7ef7ebb, the locale pin no longer applies to argv reads, but the process birth identity and SDK startup issues remain from the earlier review.

Could the host-kit observation owner emit one locale- and timezone-independent birth identity with provenance? A daemon registered under Pacific/Kiritimati and stopped under UTC gets different C-shaped lstart strings for the same PID, and the classifier treats the shared shape as a shared clock. The exit wait can report exit before signaling, so detached stop can report not-running and retire a live daemon's lock and metadata. Claim, lock, and managed-process observations also treat the difference as reuse. Old raw POSIX values need to remain unknown unless the lifetime is independently established. [Identity classifier](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/7ef7ebb/packages/host-kit/src/internal/ps-start-time.ts#L64)

Could every live signal authorization gate require a positive match between comparable birth identities, with command matching independent? A recycled PID can have the same raw local-second string under a different timezone, bypass the mismatch check, and pass the daemon entry-path check. That can authorize a signal to a different process lifetime. Legacy raw POSIX values need to remain unknown for equality too. [Signal gate](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/7ef7ebb/packages/daemon-contracts/src/daemon-process.ts#L38)

Could scoped and unscoped launch and observation routes use the same clock, with the captured host bound at declared entrypoints for probes that need its environment? An unscoped lstart probe receives only LC_ALL=C, while Node ensureDaemon passes the captured TZ to the child. With a nondefault TZ, the parent can reject its live child during readiness. The scoped real-child test does not cover this route. Please verify a fresh Node ensureDaemon call with a nondefault TZ. [Probe environment](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/7ef7ebb/packages/host-kit/src/internal/exec.ts#L171)

Could the Unicode test remove the self-comparison and retain the environment-sensitive reader regression and real-child stop test? It supplies the same constructed argv to both sides without invoking ps, so it stays green with the earlier overbroad pin. [Test](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/7ef7ebb/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.test.ts#L226)

Could the valid and stale process birth fixtures be shared in test-kit? The same values appear in three test files, so each identity format change requires three updates. [Fixture](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/7ef7ebb/packages/platform-web/src/agent-browser-lifecycle.test.ts#L16)

Could you attach exact-head macOS receipts for the CLI and recording routes? The takeover test uses a stub process and synthetic timestamps, and the progress comment reports partial real macOS validation without the underlying transcript. At the fixed SHA, start a detached daemon in a fresh state directory under fr_FR.UTF-8, record its PID and birth identity, and run daemon stop --state-dir <dir> --json under LC_TIME=C; show stopped:true, mode:graceful, and that PID exiting. Repeat with different explicit TZ values, and show a fresh Node ensureDaemon call under a nondefault TZ recognizing its child. For a genuine pre-fix non-C registration, show details.terminationReason=identity-unverified, the live PID, and retained metadata and lock. Through an Apple simulator daemon session, run record start and record stop and show the recorder exiting and its owned resource released. Include the SHA, commands, and outputs. [Takeover test](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/7ef7ebb/packages/daemon-contracts/src/daemon-process-takeover.test.ts#L182)

Not blocking: the stale CIM fixtures could use valid distinct 21-digit samples, the Unicode child test could bind an installed UTF-8 locale, the stop regression could use a recorded nb_NO.UTF-8 dotted-clock value, and the redundant one-second reuse test could be removed; please take or leave these suggestions.

Could comparable POSIX identities live in the already loaded host-kit process capability alongside the Linux and Windows producers, with sync and async paths sharing one probe policy and the existing exec resolver owning spawn overrides? Could argv reads stay separate, qualified observations yield positive and negative lifetime judgments, and the extra eager import be collapsed? First, the canonical POSIX clock, provenance discriminator, and unknown legacy behavior for both matches and differences need definitions; saved-state structural equality should remain intact. Apple snapshot provider routing can stay separate, and no ADR amendment is needed.

The Coverage failure most likely comes from the added eager module, since its inbound static imports remain; please confirm from the job log. No conflicts are known. Before merge, please fix birth identity and the unscoped SDK route, repair the regressions and eager closure growth at their source, and provide passing exact-head checks and the macOS receipts above.

Round 2 at head `ea5c816b274e7fb88e0b4fabb441df5c164f86b2` (single fast-forward `7ef7ebb7d4..ea5c816b27`, no force-push).

**Eager-closure / Coverage failure — fixed at the seam, no baseline changes.** The `ps-start-time` module is deleted and its logic now lives in the already-loaded `host-process.ts` (984 lines, under the 1000 cap). `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit-core scripts/__tests__/eager-closure-budgets.test.ts` passes (909/909); the full receipt below shows `vitest-related` passed and zero eager-closure failures — the Coverage job's "adds 1 module" finding is gone.

**Cross-TZ identity — closed with provenanced birth tokens.** New POSIX reads canonicalize the pinned C-form `lstart` (parsed in the reader's zone) to `posix:<epochMs>`, a zone-independent token with explicit comparable provenance. `processStartTimesDiffer` proves a different lifetime only between two tokens of the same provenanced format (`linux:`, `posix:`, 21-digit Windows CIM); historical raw renderings — localized and raw C-form alike — are unqualified, so they yield `identity-unverified`: never `already-exited`, never a signal. `isAgentDeviceDaemonProcess` requires a provenanced expected token plus exact match plus command match. Linux `/proc` and Windows CIM routes, unpinned argv reads (UTF-8 command text preserved; only `lstart=`-bearing reads pin `LC_ALL=C` via `envOverrides`), and cancellation are unchanged. No shutdown-transport or signal-scope expansion.

**Live macOS verification at exact head `ea5c816b27`** (disposable daemons, per-process env only, no host-global settings, owner-proven cleanup, no leftover daemons):
- Cross-locale: daemon started under `LC_ALL=fr_FR.UTF-8` recorded `processStartTime: "posix:1795036084000"`; `LC_ALL=C LC_TIME=C agent-device daemon stop --json` → `stopped: true, mode: "graceful"`, pid 69017 gone, state dir cleaned.
- Cross-TZ: daemon started under `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` recorded `posix:1795036104000` while raw `lstart` rendered `Thu Nov 19 11:08:24 2026` there vs `Wed Nov 18 21:08:24 2026` under `TZ=UTC`; stop under `TZ=UTC LC_ALL=C` → `stopped: true, mode: "graceful"`, pid 70294 gone.
- Legacy record: raw C-form `Wed Nov 18 22:08:42 2026` written into a live daemon's `daemon.json` (pid 71455); `LC_ALL=C daemon stop --json` → `success: false`, `terminationReason: "identity-unverified"`, `removedInfo: false`, `daemon.json` + `daemon.lock` retained, pid still alive. Owner cleanup (SIGTERM) confirmed the pid gone and the state dir removed.

**Checks receipt:** `pnpm check:affected --run --head ea5c816b274e7fb88e0b4fabb441df5c164f86b2` → receipt `.tmp/validation/run-s0JGzn/receipt.json`, `exactCommit=true`: format, lint, typecheck, layering, fallow, build, vitest-related all **passed**; `unit` failed only on 6 load-induced flakes while a concurrent validation ran on this host (release-publish ×4, snapshot-helper-exit-result ×1, macos-helper-package-contents ×1) — all 3 files pass in isolation (40/40), and none are touched by this PR; the pre-existing baseline failures (eager-closure-budgets ×65, daemon-process-takeover) are gone. `pnpm format` clean, `pnpm build` green, frozen lockfile install used throughout.

No device proof was run — no device is assigned to this task via T3. Not merged, not watched; readiness labels untouched.

Round 3 at head `0b301eefcaac49c597faab47667f9c2303fe2de1` (single fast-forward `ea5c816b27..0b301eefca`).

**UTC clock at the lstart-only ownership seam.** The lstart-bearing ps probes now override `TZ=UTC` alongside `LC_ALL=C`, applied as the final `envOverrides` word in `resolveSpawnEnv` — so a captured host/request TZ can no longer change the zone the ps child renders in, and the rest of the effective child env (and unpinned argv reads) is untouched. The known UTC output is parsed with `Date.UTC`, so the `posix:<epochMs>` token no longer depends on the JS reader's local zone and DST folds are out of scope. Scoped and unscoped routes share this one probe policy; Linux `/proc` and Windows CIM producers, cancellation, and the eager-closure shape (no new module) are unchanged. Legacy raw POSIX values remain unqualified → `identity-unverified` for both equality and difference; the signal gate still requires a provenanced token plus exact match plus command match. New regression test: a C-form read canonicalizes identically with the reader process under `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` vs baseline.

**SDK ensureDaemon under nondefault TZ, differing parent TZ** (fresh Node `ensureDaemon` from `@agent-device/daemon-client`, per-process env only, disposable state dirs, owner-proven cleanup):
- `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati node --experimental-strip-types .tmp/ensure-r3.ts` → `{"readerTZ":"Pacific/Kiritimati","started":true,"pid":49006,"token":"posix:1795037630000"}` — the parent recognized its own live child during readiness under a nondefault captured TZ.
- `TZ=UTC …` same state dir → `started:false, pid:49006, token:"posix:1795037630000"`; `TZ=America/New_York LC_ALL=fr_FR.UTF-8 …` → `started:false`, same pid/token. Differing parent TZ attaches without replacing the daemon.
- That SDK-started daemon was then stopped via `TZ=Europe/Paris LC_ALL=C daemon stop --json` → `stopped:true, mode:"graceful"`, pid 49006 exited; state dir removed; no leftover daemons.

**Exact-head CLI + legacy receipts at `0b301eefca`** (retained from this round's runs):
- Cross-locale: daemon under `LC_ALL=fr_FR.UTF-8` recorded `posix:1795037566000` (pid 45677); raw lstart rendered `mer. 18 nov. 22:32:46 2026` (fr_FR) / `Wed Nov 18 21:32:46 2026` (C,UTC) / `Thu Nov 19 11:32:46 2026` (Kiritimati) — one instant; `LC_ALL=C LC_TIME=C daemon stop --json` → `stopped:true, mode:"graceful"`, pid exited.
- Cross-TZ: daemon under `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` recorded `posix:1795037598000` (pid 47318); stop under `TZ=UTC LC_ALL=C` → `stopped:true, mode:"graceful"`, pid exited.
- Legacy no-signal: raw C-form `Wed Nov 18 21:33:21 2026` written into a live daemon's `daemon.json` (pid 47518, real token `posix:1795037601000`); `LC_ALL=C daemon stop --json` → `success:false`, `terminationReason:"identity-unverified"`, `removedInfo:false`, `daemon.json`+`daemon.lock` retained, pid alive; owner SIGTERM cleanup confirmed pid gone, dir removed.

**Checks at exact head:** `pnpm check:affected --run --head 0b301eefcaac49c597faab47667f9c2303fe2de1` → receipt `.tmp/validation/run-smaLfc/receipt.json`, `exactCommit=true`: format, lint, typecheck, layering, fallow, build, vitest-related **passed**; unit = 20592 passed / 2 failed, both in files this PR does not touch (`scripts/__tests__/release-publish.test.ts`, `test/repo-guards/macos-helper-package-contents.test.ts`) — release-publish also fails on the pristine 70f0b17 baseline, and both files pass in isolation at this head (8/8), so they are environmental, not regressions; eager-closure-budgets is green (909/909 direct, and inside the passing vitest-related/unit scope). Host-global state untouched: all runs used per-process env on disposable daemons only.

**Still pending (reported separately, not done):** the Apple-simulator recording route receipt (`record start`/`record stop` through a simulator daemon session, recorder exit + owned-resource release). No device is assigned to this task via T3, so no simulator was touched. Not merged, not watched; labels untouched.

**Exact-head recording verification — PASS**

- Candidate: `0b301eefcaac49c597faab47667f9c2303fe2de1` (PR head), checked out and built in a clean worktree (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm build:xcuitest:ios`); CLI reports `0.21.40-dev`, daemon `codeOrigin: checkout`. Working tree clean afterward — no source changes.
- Device: iPhone 17 Pro Max simulator, iOS 27.0, UDID `DBEA214F-555F-4DDA-B62B-E34285CE63DB`, host `local`. `device_open` succeeded with no `DEVICE_IN_USE` or foreign claim; the Device panel open-list contained only this verification thread. Device left booted, as found.
- Runner: the T3 device-bound CLI is pinned to published `0.21.36` and cannot execute the candidate, so per the device instructions the repo-owned recording test runner `test/integration/recording-contact-sheet.test.ts` (`node --test`, `AGENT_DEVICE_RECORDING_E2E=1`, `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_UDID=<udid>`) was used; it executes this checkout's own `src/bin.ts` at the candidate SHA against the assigned simulator. Result: **pass 1, fail 0** (~28 s).
- Exercised on the assigned simulator: `open com.apple.Preferences --relaunch` → `record start <out>.mp4` → `click` / `scroll down` / `back` → `record stop` (success, exit 0) → `record contact-sheet`. Export `contact-sheet.mp4` written (3,540,793 bytes) with PNG contact sheet and gesture-telemetry sidecar (artifacts under gitignored `test/artifacts/ios/record-contact-sheet/...`).
- Recorder exit / owned-resource release: session manifest `screen-recording.resource.json` shows `lifecycle: "completed"`, `phase: "completed"`, `stopObservation.recorder: "confirmed"`, `nativePathDisposition: "retired"`. The recorder (`simctl io <udid> recordVideo`, pid 66761) was recorded with birth token `posix:1795039280000` — the new pinned-UTC `lstart` canonical form from this PR — and that pid is gone after `record stop`; no `recordVideo` process remains and no `owned-processes.json` is left in the session state dir. The test daemon itself registered `processStartTime: "posix:1795039265000"` through the same probe.
- Cleanup: the test session ran `close` (session events end with `close`); the test daemon (pid 65558) was reaped at runner teardown and is no longer alive; the foreground app was restored to `com.callstack.agentdevicelab` through the device-bound CLI and that panel session was closed without `--shutdown` (the simulator was already booted and stays booted).

Limit: a manual record start/stop through the T3 device-bound CLI was not used as evidence, because that CLI runs published `0.21.36`, not this head; all candidate proof above comes from the repo-owned runner executing the candidate source.

I reviewed 0b301ee against the earlier review (https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4682#issuecomment-6991549249). The new design is closer, but the safety rule still has gaps and it changes the saved identity format for registrations that already exist. CI is still running with no failures reported yet. No conflicts. Before merge, the shared proof and format-change problems below need fixes, the tests need to exercise the real read path, and the exact-head macOS transcripts need to be attached.

When the host returns the same unparseable raw lstart as the saved record, [host-process.ts:413](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/0b301ee/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.ts#L413) keeps the raw text and the shared stop judge returns ours on string equality. Recorder termination and owned-process reaping use the same check, and the daemon-only guard at daemon-process.ts:39 does not cover them. An unqualified clock rendering can then authorize a signal with no positive proof of the recorded lifetime. Please have host-kit expose one match/different/unknown comparison, and let only its match result open every PID-based signal gate that uses a birth marker. Keep raw equality only for structural fences, and keep direct child handles as independent evidence.

The stop test stub at [host-process-stop-confirm.test.ts:236](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/0b301ee/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process-stop-confirm.test.ts#L236) emits an already encoded posix token in the ps row (:303-316). At 7ef7ebb the classifier already treated that token and a raw C value as incomparable, so the test can pass without this change. The mixed cases in host-process.test.ts:199 and owner-identity-liveness.test.ts:64 bypass the reader the same way, and so does the daemon case at daemon-metadata-loss.test.ts:98. These routes can look protected while the reader still emits raw lstart or the signal gate still accepts raw equality. Please make the ps stub emit C-form lstart and keep the saved fixture independent. Cover a differing raw C value that 7ef7ebb treats as reassignment, and separately an identical unqualified read and record that sends no signal.

The latest live results are from ea5c816b27, but this head changes the child clock and parser ([host-process.ts:239](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/0b301ee/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.ts#L239)). Please attach commands, outputs and the SHA for a real detached CLI daemon in a fresh state directory across French/C locales and differing TZ values, showing the token, a graceful stop and the PID exit. Add a fresh unscoped Node ensureDaemon with nondefault TZ that recognizes its child. For a genuine pre-fix non-C registration, show identity-unverified with a live PID and retained lock and metadata. For an Apple simulator daemon session, show record start/stop, recorder PID exit and release of the recording resource.

Under the same locale and settings, a healthy pre-fix macOS Metro companion has a raw saved startTime. The new probe returns posix, so reuse fails at [client-companion-tunnel.ts:246](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/0b301ee/packages/react-native/src/companion/client-companion-tunnel.ts#L246), and the ensure path at :489 tries a stop that keeps the live process as unverified at :318. After upgrade, a working tunnel becomes unusable, and a repeated ensure and an explicit stop both fail while the worker stays registered. Please give the companion lifecycle a safe upgrade path, such as owner-side shutdown before the identity change or re-verification through an independent worker-owned fence. Keep the record and fail closed when no owner can be established.

A live retained runner from before this change has a raw runnerStartTime.
